evals.prompt: We installed governance-kit into this repo months ago and the preset was wrong. I want a clean slate before re-running governance init. Run governance uninstall — remove every governance artifact this repo has, including the seeded QUALITY.md and COSTS.md (we haven't put real content in them yet). Don't touch anything else.
evals.expected_output: Following UNINSTALL_FLOW.md Steps 1–6: the skill surveys the repo, reads the install state pair (`.governance/install.yaml` v3 + `.governance/packs.lock` v2), classifies the state as `fully-installed`, asks the user for a mode (dry-run / soft / hard) via AskUserQuestion, and — given the user's 'include seeded docs' direction — proceeds in `hard` mode after explicit confirmation. It deletes every kit-owned artifact (constitution, .governance tree, CI workflow, managed hooks, install.yaml, packs.lock, AGENTS.md directive block, seeded docs). It unsets `core.hooksPath` only if it still points at `.githooks`. It leaves changes unstaged. The summary names mode, classification, source-of-truth, files deleted, files preserved, AGENTS.md outcome, git config outcome, assumptions, and `Next command: git status`.
assertions: The skill read `.governance/install.yaml` AND `.governance/packs.lock` and reported `Source of truth: manifest` (or equivalent)
The skill asked the user to choose a mode (dry-run / soft / hard) before executing
`CONSTITUTION.md` was deleted
`.governance/` was deleted recursively (run.sh, lib.sh, every directive folder under packs/<owner>/<name>/directives/<id>/, install.yaml, packs.lock all gone)
`.github/workflows/governance.yml` was deleted
`.githooks/pre-commit`, `.githooks/commit-msg`, and `.githooks/prepare-commit-msg` were deleted (each carried the line-2 `governance-kit:managed` marker)

`AGENTS.md` was edited in-place: the marker-bounded block (paired `<!-- governance: directives-to-follow -->` markers, falling back to opening-marker-only heuristic if needed) was stripped, and a byte-diff confirmed every other line is identical to the fixture
`QUALITY.md` and `COSTS.md` were deleted (hard mode, as the user requested removing seeded docs)
The skill did not run `git clean`, `git reset --hard`, `git stash`, or any destructive git operation
The skill did not auto-commit — the working tree shows the deletions as unstaged (or staged but uncommitted)
The skill ran `git config --unset core.hooksPath` only if the value still equaled `.githooks` (left it alone otherwise, with a note in the report)

The final summary names: Mode (`hard`), Classification (`fully-installed`), Source of truth (`manifest`), Files deleted, Files preserved, AGENTS.md outcome, Git config outcome, and `Next command: git status`

evals.prompt: This repo has no governance setup. Run governance uninstall.
evals.expected_output: Following UNINSTALL_FLOW.md Step 2's `none-detected` classification: the skill surveys the repo, finds no manifest, no managed hooks, no `CONSTITUTION.md`, no `.governance/` — classifies as `none-detected` — and reports 'nothing to remove' without asking for a mode. No files are modified. Idempotency contract: running uninstall on a clean repo is a success, not an error.
assertions: No files were created, deleted, or modified in the fixture
The skill classified the repo as `none-detected` (or equivalent wording)
The skill exited without asking the user for a mode, because there is nothing to mode-select over
The skill's final message tells the user the repo has no governance-kit footprint

evals.prompt: Run governance uninstall. But only show me the plan — don't delete anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Following UNINSTALL_FLOW.md Step 3: the skill runs the full survey and builds the execute plan, then honors the user's explicit dry-run request by printing the plan without executing. The working tree is byte-identical before and after. The summary is prefixed with 'would-' verbs so it is unambiguous that nothing happened.
assertions: No files were deleted or modified in the fixture
The skill explicitly chose `dry-run` mode (the user's request made the default obvious; no AskUserQuestion needed)
The summary lists the files that *would* be deleted, not files that were deleted
The summary's mode field reads `dry-run`
Git config was not mutated (`core.hooksPath` left as-is)

evals.prompt: I want to remove governance from this repo but soft-mode only — keep my QUALITY.md and COSTS.md, those are real docs now.
evals.expected_output: Following UNINSTALL_FLOW.md Step 5: the skill executes in `soft` mode after confirmation. Pack-seeded docs (`QUALITY.md`, `COSTS.md`) are preserved and reported as orphaned. Every other kit-owned artifact is deleted. The summary makes the soft-vs-hard distinction explicit so the user understands which files were intentionally kept.
assertions: `QUALITY.md` and `COSTS.md` still exist after uninstall (preserved per soft-mode contract)
`CONSTITUTION.md`, `.governance/`, `.github/workflows/governance.yml`, and the marked `.githooks/*` files were deleted
The summary's `Files preserved:` line names `QUALITY.md` and `COSTS.md` as soft-mode orphans
The summary's `Mode:` field reads `soft`
The skill did not auto-commit
